A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GRIDDD, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures, algorithms and appendices. Reorganized and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original molecular property-targeting, optimization, out-of-distribution and ablation results on QM9 and ZINC-250k.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds padding comparisons, sampling-time measurements, EDM-SyCO comparisons, sensitivity tests and failure analysis.

M1.justification: The architecture, DEL/DEL* mechanism, activation-time prediction, auxiliary network, loss and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. Corrections to the sampling formulas align them with v1's stated probability and absolute-distance descriptions; the PDFs do not establish a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use QM9 and ZINC-250k for the same molecular generation, targeting, optimization and graph-size extrapolation tasks. The added studies vary evaluation procedures, budgets and model settings within this coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds actual comparisons against EDM-SyCO for optimization and molecular-weight targeting, plus NodesPAD and AllPAD alternatives in Table 4. These substantially extend the comparison set. CG-VAE remains in Table 3 for LogP and QED, but its DRD2 comparison entry disappears.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a separate optimization protocol with 100 candidates per round, top-ten selection and four rounds, alongside a 1000-timestep molecular-weight experiment. Other additions include diversity metrics, a 250-epoch padding comparison, and timing 128 samples under different latent initializations. The original benchmark protocols and dataset splits are retained.

E4.justification: V2 tests whether padding can substitute for explicit insertion/deletion, studies sensitivity to four scheduler/node-count parameters, and analyzes sampling speed across latent initializations. Appendices A.2 and D.4 additionally report qualitative label-distribution comparisons and failures near zero dipole moment. The original disabled-edit ablation and out-of-distribution analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use the existing plus/minus reporting convention without newly specifying seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Additional candidate-generation rounds are evaluation-budget changes, not independent repetitions for uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the shared GRIDDD optimization scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds diversity, padding, timing and sensitivity results. Under the new multi-round protocol, Table 6 reports QED success of 64.1% versus EDM-SyCO's 46.4%, but DRD2 success of 19.7% versus 27.3%. These are additional results under different conditions, not improvements over v1's original protocol. CG-VAE's 2.3% DRD2 entry becomes unreported.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 correct the probability expressions by introducing absolute values, including |n−n0| in the node-count distribution. Appendix B.4 adds mathematical reasoning about node-dependent edge transitions and the independence assumption. The main posterior derivation is retained, with no new theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution and performance claims: size-adaptive discrete graph diffusion with competitive property targeting and optimization. Additional evidence does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of near-zero-dipole failures, sampling speed through smaller intermediate tensors, and sensitivity of disconnected molecules to insertion timing. It also discusses adjacency-power features as a possible mitigation and acknowledges node–edge dependence in Appendix B.4. The original simultaneous-edit and disconnected-molecule limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a repository URL, explains caching per-molecule label distributions, and documents settings for the new studies. Existing architecture, pseudocode, splits and hardware disclosures largely remain. V1's explicit instruction to disable insertions/deletions during the initial optimization corruption is omitted; this omission does not establish a procedural change.

R1.justification: V2 adds Campbell et al.'s trans-dimensional jump diffusion and distinguishes its capabilities from GRIDDD. It also cites Liu et al. for the already-evaluated CG-VAE baseline and expands positioning against the previously cited Ketata et al. method. The broader related-work framework remains stable.

P1.justification: The supplementary material is systematically reorganized into methodology, experimental details, computational considerations and additional results, with the checklist moved before the appendices. V2 also adds a computational subsection and rewrites the deletion-state explanation. This substantially changes document organization despite retaining most of the main narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adds four tables, expands Table 3 with diversity columns, and redraws Figure 3 as a wider plot with an explicit legend. V1's numerical out-of-distribution table is removed while its results remain plotted. Scheduler, architecture and molecule illustrations are retained but relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central contribution by testing a simpler padding alternative and directly comparing with EDM-SyCO under explicitly described protocols. Sensitivity, failure and timing analyses clarify practical strengths and weaknesses, while formula corrections improve mathematical accuracy. Removing the numerical out-of-distribution table and the corruption-setting instruction loses some detail, but these limited losses are outweighed by the stronger evaluation and explanation.
